subject: general
question: A person stands 36 metres away from the foot of a tower. The angle of elevation to the top of the tower is theta , and tantheta = 5/3 . What is the height (in metres) of the tower?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Height : Distance from foot = 5 : 3

Given, distance (3 units) = 36 m

1 unit = 36 / 3 = 12 m

Height (5 units) = 5 × 12 = 60 m

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Distance of person from tower foot (Base) = 36 m

Angle of elevation = θ, where tan θ = 5/3

Formula: tan θ = Perpendicular (Height) / Base (Distance)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/127b213bd8fd1e2a5670696778b942b606d0ff85d6a489457076cd7575d99f3e.png] 

⇒ tan θ = Height / 36

⇒ 5 / 3 = Height / 36

⇒ Height = (5 × 36) / 3

⇒ Height = 5 × 12

⇒ Height = 60 m

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular/Base, sin θ = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse, and cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse.

Angle of Elevation

It is the angle between the horizontal line and the line of sight when an observer looks at an object above the horizontal level.

Pythagoras Theorem

For a right triangle with height h and base b, the hypotenuse l is given by l = √(h² + b²).
